blocks.text: Why AI tool implementation is difficult for executive assistants

Implementation is hard because most tools lack context. They do not know your executive's preferences, the office politics, or the nuances of your specific industry. When you try to automate too much, you lose the human touch that makes you valuable. Many EAs also struggle with tool fatigue. You have too many apps already. Adding another AI subscription often feels like more work, not less.
The hidden costs of poor AI adoption

The biggest cost is time. You spend hours learning a new tool that does not actually save you time. Another cost is security. If you paste confidential documents into a public AI model, you risk a data leak. This can lead to disciplinary action or the loss of trust with your executive. Finally, there is the cost of error correction. If the AI makes a mistake in an email to a board member, you are the one who has to fix it. This creates more work, not less.
How can executive assistants use ai safely

Start by using AI for drafting, not for decision making. Use it to expand bullet points into a professional email draft. Use it to summarize long threads. Never use it to manage sensitive personnel data unless your company has an approved, private instance of the AI. Always treat the output as a draft. You are the final editor. If you work in a regulated field like law or finance, ensure your usage complies with your company's data handling policy.
Practical fixes for your daily Mac workflow

items: Use local dictation to draft emails quickly.
Create templates for common responses and use AI to customize them.
Use AI to summarize meeting notes and extract action items.
Maintain a document with your executive's preferred writing style.
Keep your AI usage transparent with your manager.

blocks.text: Lazur is a voice assistant that lives in your Mac notch. It helps you get work done faster without leaving your current app. You hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask questions about your screen. It can explain what a button does or point at it for you. You can hold fn to dictate text directly into your documents. It keeps your data on your Mac, which helps with security.
